_comment: Approved calibration notes from the /reflect loop. The reflection pass PROPOSES changes; nothing here is auto-written — Sam adds an entry after approving a proposal. global_notes apply to every role; company_notes[company] apply only to that company. These are appended to the scoring prompt as guidance.
global_notes: Level strategy (Sam, June 2026; Google added to at-level tier 2026-06-18): Sam currently works at Amazon (AWS) as a Sr. GTM/Sales-Ops Manager (~L6). He will only LEAVE Amazon for a non-Amazon company if the move is either (a) to a company he wants on its own terms — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Google DeepMind — where joining AT-LEVEL is acceptable, or (b) a genuine LEVEL-UP in scope/seniority over his current L6 role. For every OTHER external company (Databricks, NVIDIA, Snowflake, CoreWeave, and any future target outside the at-level tier), only roles that represent an up-level (Head / Director / Principal / Lead / GM with real org or charter scope, or a clearly broader mandate than he holds today) should reach Strong or Perfect; down-tier roles that are merely lateral (another Sr Manager / L6-equivalent IC) or lower cap at AT MOST Good Match, even when domain and role-type fit are excellent, and the rationale states the cap is seniority/level, not fit. EXEMPTIONS from the level-up requirement: Amazon internal transfers (lateral L6 is fine, see Amazon note) and the AT-LEVEL TIER — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Google DeepMind — where a lateral is acceptable: score on genuine fit and do NOT cap a strong-fit role at Good merely for being lateral / a 'Manager' title; let it reach Strong or Perfect when domain + role-type + seniority-scope fit are there.

Dimension calibration for Sam's NON-ENGINEERING target roles (set 2026-06-18 after Sam flagged generic-qualification GTM roles scoring too low on role_type/technical fit): Sam's target archetypes — GTM Systems & Agents, AI Product Strategy & Growth, Applied AI (customer-outcome), Strategy & Operations, Business/Partner Strategy, Chief of Staff with scope — are intentionally non-engineering. Two corrections: (1) technical_fit must measure whether Sam clears the role's ACTUAL technical bar, NOT whether the role is technical. Strategy/GTM/ops roles have a generic bar (analytics, data fluency, exec comms, light SQL) that Sam EXCEEDS — he also ships production AI systems — so technical_fit for such roles should be HIGH (78-90), never penalized for the role being non-technical. (2) role_type_fit: genuine GTM-strategy / strategy-and-operations / business-strategy / partner-strategy / product-strategy roles ARE Sam's target types — score them as STRONG role-type fit (78-90). Do NOT dock them to the 50s for 'operating an existing motion / cadences / exec decks / partnership facilitation' rather than '0->1 build.' The 0->1-AI-builder shape is his PREFERRED flavor and can reach Perfect; an operating/strategy GTM role he qualifies for is still a STRONG fit, not Good (net: low-to-mid 80s). This does NOT license inflating truly off-target roles: recruiting/finance/facilities ops, pure program-coordination with no strategy charter, quota-carrying sales, or engineering/solutions-architect roles still score on their real (lower) fit.

Years-of-experience criteria (Sam, Aug 2026): Do NOT penalize a role for a stated years-of-experience minimum that exceeds Sam's ~12 years. Posted YoE minimums are inflated, negotiable screening numbers — they gauge capability/scope, not literal tenure. If a role asks for '15 years' (or any number above Sam's 12) but the DOMAIN, ROLE-TYPE, and SCOPE/LEVEL fit, treat the YoE requirement as MET — do NOT dock seniority_fit or overall_score for the year-count gap alone, and do NOT cite 'X years required vs 12' as a gap. Judge seniority_fit on scope/level/charter fit (does the role's altitude match what he operates at), never on the literal year count. This is a de-emphasis of one criterion only; genuine scope/level mismatches (e.g. a VP/GM mandate far above his level) still count normally.

Partnerships / ecosystem GTM is a CONVERTIBLE archetype for Sam (Aug 2026): Sam spent 5.5+ years in AWS Startups running partner / startup-ecosystem GTM (Activate programs, partner enablement, startup-to-partner motions), and 'AI Partnerships' is an explicit target_role_type. So PARTNER / STARTUP / AI-PARTNERSHIPS GTM roles are his convertible archetype, NOT generic relationship-BD. Do NOT dock role_type_fit into the 50s for 'relationship-driven / partner BD / ecosystem management' language on these — his background IS partner-ecosystem GTM. Score role_type_fit as STRONG (75-88) for roles like Startup Partnerships Lead, AI/GenAI Partner GTM, Worldwide Partner Specialist, partner-GTM-strategy — where the work is developing partner GTM strategy, driving partner/ISV adoption, and building partner motions (his exact AWS Startups experience). NOT a blanket boost: pure channel/quota partner SALES, reseller-quota, or relationship-only account-management roles with no strategy/build scope still score on their real (lower) fit.

ML-RESEARCH product roles require pedigree Sam lacks (Aug 2026): Sam's fit is APPLIED AI / AI Product Strategy & Growth / GTM / customer-outcome product work PLUS hands-on AI BUILDING — NOT ML research. Roles that are research-facing or gated on ML-research / model-science depth — 'Research Product Manager', 'Product Management, Research', 'Model Behaviors', 'Pretraining', research-scientist-adjacent PM, or roles owning a research roadmap / model capabilities / evals-as-research — are NOT his background; they screen on published research, model-training experience, and ML depth he does not have. Do NOT score these as domain_fit or role_type_fit 90+, and do NOT let them reach Perfect for Sam. Cap at MODERATE fit (Good, ~70-79; low-Strong only if there is a genuine applied-AI / GTM / product-strategy angle), and note the research-pedigree gap. This does NOT temper APPLIED AI / AI-product-strategy / 0->1 AI product / agentic-product / GTM roles — those remain his targets and can reach Strong/Perfect. The distinction is ML-research / model-science (NOT his) vs applied-AI-product / GTM / strategy (his).

EVIDENCED vs ASPIRATIONAL archetypes (Sam, Aug 2026 - set after Sam flagged that Product Manager roles were topping the board despite him never having held a PM title). Sam's target_role_types in profile.json MIX roles he has direct evidence in with roles he aspires to. Score the two differently. (1) EVIDENCED - score at full strength, may reach Strong or Perfect: GTM strategy and operations, product/business strategy and operations, market and competitive intelligence, executive decision systems, chief-of-staff-with-build-scope, GTM systems and agents, and applied-AI work with a GTM or customer-outcome flavor. This is his actual job and his AWS record backs it. (2) ASPIRATIONAL - CAP AT GOOD MATCH (70-79): roles whose core mandate is owning a product as a Product Manager (titles like 'Product Manager', 'Senior Product Manager', 'Group Product Manager', 'Principal Product Manager', 'Head of Product', 'Director of Product') where the job is roadmap ownership, specs, launch, and engineering/design partnership rather than strategy and operations. Sam has NO formal Product Manager title (see locked facts). He is a credible candidate for these but not an evidenced one, so they must NOT reach Strong or Perfect and must NOT top the board. State the reason in the rationale: 'capped at Good - no formal PM title; aspirational archetype, not an evidenced one.' (3) BRIDGE EXCEPTION - may reach Strong, still not Perfect: a role carrying a PM title whose described scope is actually product STRATEGY and OPERATIONS, GTM or market intelligence, or which explicitly welcomes strategy/consulting/non-traditional backgrounds. Shapes like 'Product Strategy and Operations Principal/Lead' or 'Product and Business Strategy Lead' are hybrids and sit close to what he does. PRECEDENCE: this note OVERRIDES any company note instructing that 'AI-native product PM' or similar be scored as STRONG role-type fit (the Google note does say this). Company notes still govern which DOMAINS are on target; this note governs the PM-title ceiling. NOT a blanket demotion: it does not touch Strategy and Operations, GTM, partnerships, chief-of-staff, or applied-AI-with-GTM-flavor roles. Those stay full-strength and are where Sam's supply of Strong and Perfect matches should come from.

Databricks: Target-role signal (Databricks, June 2026): Sam targets AI Product Strategy & Growth, Applied AI (customer-outcome), GTM Systems & Agents, and Chief-of-Staff-with-build-scope roles on the data + AI platform (e.g. Lead/Principal PM for Mosaic AI / Agents, Head of GTM Strategy & Ops, Applied AI Lead). Score these as STRONG role-type fit, not generic big-co PM/ops. As a step-out from Amazon, apply the global level rule: only an up-level over L6 (Head/Director/Principal/Lead with real scope) reaches Strong/Perfect; lateral Sr-Manager/IC roles cap at Good Match regardless of domain fit. Do NOT inflate engineering / solutions-architect / sales-engineering / pure quota-ops roles.

Amazon: Saved-roles signal (Amazon internal, June 2026): Sam's own shortlist shows his top Amazon targets are L6 WWSO GenAI / Data & AI GTM Specialist and Worldwide/Partner Specialist roles (e.g. GenAI-Bedrock, Agentic AI - Kiro & Frontier Agents, Foundation Models, Accelerate Compute), plus Partner Development Manager, GenAI Strategist (Startups), and Deal Intelligence/Automation PMT. Score these L6 GTM / Partner-Specialist / Strategist GenAI roles as STRONG role-type fit (they are his GTM Systems & Agents / Applied AI / AI Product Growth targets with a GTM flavor) rather than capping them at the 'GTM execution = Strong' band - they should reach Perfect when domain and seniority also fit. Internal transfer at L6 is a lateral move (no up-level friction). Do NOT blanket-inflate unrelated Amazon roles (engineering/SA, non-AI infrastructure, pure planning/quota ops).
Google: Target-role signal (Google, June 2026): Sam targets GTM Strategy & Operations, Product Strategy & Growth, Applied AI / AI-native product PM, and Chief-of-Staff-with-build-scope roles at Google (e.g. 'Strategy and Operations Lead/Principal, GTM', 'Product Strategy and Operations Principal, Cloud AI', 'Global Product Lead, GTM Intelligence/Optimization', 'PM, Applied AI' / 'AI-Native Product Development'). Score these GTM-Strategy / Applied-AI / Product-Growth roles as STRONG role-type fit - they are his GTM Systems & Agents / AI Product Strategy & Growth / Applied AI targets, not generic big-co coordination. When domain (AI / GTM / customer-and-product signal) and seniority (Lead / Principal / Head) also fit, let them reach Strong or Perfect rather than pinning them at the big-company 84 cap or a 'GTM execution = Good' band. Do NOT blanket-inflate unrelated Google roles (ads/sales quota ops, recruiting, finance, non-AI infrastructure, engineering / solutions-architect, pure program coordination).
